heroes.assetName: Chapter 1 hero – Moon Jar (procedural 3D arrives in Phase 3)

alt.text: Placeholder frame for the Moon Jar hero

direction.text: Frame luxury strictly through restraint and the Korean Moon Jar as an artistic muse.

beats.text: When Genesis set out to build their most ambitious car, the hardest part wasn't what to add. It was what to remove.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 1

beats.text: Strip away everything that distracts, and you are left with nothing to hide behind
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 1

beats.text: Every curve has to carry meaning on its own
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 1

beats.text: To make something that would never age, they focused on form itself.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 1

beats.text: Has this been pulled off before? Yes.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 1

beats.text: The Korean Moon Jar is 300 years old. Auctioned for millions, displayed in the world's great museums, and yet no ornamentation. Just pure form doing all the work.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 1
beats.note: Factual claim about the Moon Jar (age, auction value, museums); not a GV90 spec but still needs verifying.

beats.text: This builds on the design language that Genesis has always followed.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 1

direction.text: Connect Moon Jar minimalism to physical execution: laser-etched lamps, invisible rear spoiler, and porcelain glaze paint.

beats.text: The rear spoiler, the thing that tames lift and drag, had to do the impossible by becoming invisible.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 2 › Rear Profile & Invisible Spoiler

beats.text: They went to work on the rear body curvature itself, refining it millimeter by millimeter until it could do a spoiler’s job without touching the design.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 2 › Rear Profile & Invisible Spoiler

beats.text: The result: The car could perform as if it had a spoiler without one, and kept the purity of its design intact. The spoiler was gone, but the design demanded more minimising.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 2 › Rear Profile & Invisible Spoiler

beats.text: Form without compromise.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 2 › Laser-Etched Headlights / Lamps

beats.text: Body-integrated lamps that seamlessly blend into the front and rear, conveying strength and grandeur.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 2 › Laser-Etched Headlights / Lamps

beats.text: They painted the entire lens in the body colour. Then, using a laser, we precisely carved away only the lap area.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 2 › Laser-Etched Headlights / Lamps
beats.note: Source typo kept verbatim: 'lap area' is probably 'lamp area'. Voice also shifts from 'They' to 'we'.

beats.text: The gaps are still there, but engineered so finely that the eye simply can’t find them.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 2 › Laser-Etched Headlights / Lamps

direction.text: Position the GV90 as the emerging icon of the Genesis brand.

beats.text: The vision that captivated the world now has a name, a commanding scale, and a presence that redefines flagship electric luxury.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL1 › Module 3
beats.note: Sits inside a direction bullet ('Position the GV90 as…'); read here as copy. Confirm with creative.

alt.text: The vehicle with both doors open against a sunset, the cabin backlit

heroes.note: Reused from the prologue as a stand-in until a Chapter 2 still is supplied.

direction.text: Ground the open doors in Son-nim (treating passengers as honored guests) and the feeling of a red-carpet entrance.

beats.text: From the early stages of development, we all agreed that as a flagship, we needed to approach this not merely as a 'car', but as a 'space'.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL2 › Module 1 › The Red Carpet Entry

beats.text: When both doors opened, fully exposing the space between them, we wanted to give customers the feeling of stepping off a red carpet.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL2 › Module 1 › The Red Carpet Entry

direction.text: Focus on how moving the B-pillar inside the doors preserves pure, unbroken exterior lines and expands the spatial presence of the cabin

beats.text: Genesis didn't just restyle a door. They rewrote the paradigm of entry itself to define a new flagship standard. So how do you move a B-pillar? Simple: hide it inside the door. From the passenger's perspective, it just isn't there.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL2 › Module 2

beats.text: Compromise was never an option. What was truly important to us was a coach door where the front and rear doors open independently.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL2 › Module 2
beats.note: Coach doors are GV90 Neolun only (creative brief v1 › Key Features).

direction.text: Detail the two core engineered benefits enabled by this architecture—total acoustic/weather isolation AND uncompromised structural safety tech (hidden steel beams, impact hooks, and roof airbags).

beats.text: The B-pillar does one more thing people don't think about: keeping wind and rain and road noise where they belong, outside.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL2 › Module 3 › Benefit 1

beats.text: And because this is a flagship luxury SUV, the standard wasn't just 'keep water out'. The standard was total isolation. Silence inside a vehicle is the product of hundreds of elements working together: glass thickness, structural damping, cabin insulation, partition design, each playing its part. But the door seal is one of the most vulnerable pieces of all.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL2 › Module 3 › Benefit 1

beats.text: The Overhead Roof Airbag. Engineered specifically to deploy from the glass ceiling, surrounding the entire cabin in a protective canopy without compromising the open, panoramic view above.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL2 › Module 3 › Benefit 2
beats.note: 'World-first' roof airbag: the account team's comment on this heading links a news.com.au article (meta.sources › news-roof-airbag). Still verify against Genesis's latest spec.

beats.text: The GV90 Neolun defined a new standard of safety for the luxury flagship.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL2 › Module 3 › Benefit 2

alt.text: Placeholder frame for the interior hero

direction.text: Frame the cabin not as a traditional car interior, but as a private sanctuary and living space focused on human togetherness.

beats.text: Every car is designed to reach a destination. The GV90 began elsewhere. Its destination was inside. A place you'd never want to leave, moving or still.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 1

beats.text: We wanted to break away from conventional automotive interior design rules and create a space that warmly wraps around you.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 1

beats.text: GV90 had a seat that turned. One rotation and it’s no longer the same space– a space for connection, for being together.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 1

beats.text: Every carefully orchestrated moment, designed for connection, the space begins to pull you in deeper.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 1

label.text: Sensory High Craftsmanship & Intuitive Luxury Tech

direction.text: Combine authentic tactile materials (wool cashmere, stone slate, wood) with invisible, indirect ambient illumination and human-centered innovation.

beats.text: Our fingertips can sense a difference of a tenth of a millimeter. And in a cabin this quiet, every detail had to be worth finding.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 2

beats.text: In nature, nothing feels out of place. What you see and what you touch are telling you the same thing, and that puts you at ease into a natural state.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 2

beats.text: When you see wood, you expect the warmth of its grain; when you see stone, you expect its solid, weighty touch. Authenticity begins with the essence of a material.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 2

beats.text: The team wanted to bring this harmony of senses inside the GV90. But real materials weren't designed for a car.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 2

beats.text: Woven Wool Cashmere: Visual softness with a warmer touch.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 2 › Key Materials Summary

beats.text: Natural Stone Slate: Real stone garnishes preserved for tactile texture.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 2 › Key Materials Summary

beats.text: Real Wood: Natural grain flooring underfoot.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 2 › Key Materials Summary

beats.text: Jeweler-Cut Controls: Gem-faceted buttons and dials.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › Module 2 › Key Materials Summary
beats.note: US spelling 'Jeweler' kept verbatim; AU copy would read 'Jeweller'.

beats.text: The reason we obsessed over such minute differences was that we treated the GV90 as a work of art.
beats.ref: Creative brief v1 › PL3 › after Key Materials Summary
